newsitem.title: USA: NY-NJ Port Auth. still hopes to sell bonds this wk.
newsitem.headline: NY-NJ Port Auth. still hopes to sell bonds this wk.

text.p: The Port Authority of New York and New Jersey still wants to sell about $920 million of bonds this week but no decision has been made yet, said an official with the lead underwriter on Wednesday.
"We're focussed on trying to get it done this week," said Jim Taylor, senior vice president, Lehman Brothers.

Friday was a possible sales date, the Lehman Brothers official said, explaining the syndicate preferred to go ahead with the sale this week instead of waiting until next week, when several economic reports are due out that could impact bond prices.

Further, a number of other municipal issuers are planning sales next week, which could pose competition. For example, the New York City Municipal Finance Water Authority plans to sell $640 million of bonds during that period.

Taylor added the syndicate was hinging its decision on the responses of institutional investors, who might need more time to get their paperwork done for credit approvals, though he foresaw no problems as the bonds are rated AAA.
"We're going to get feedback today and tomorrow to see if there is still a possiblity we might go this Friday."
